title: Mass: Grams and Kilograms
seo_title: Grade 4 Mass Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Estimate, measure, record, compare and order the mass of objects using bathroom scales, kitchen scales and balances; use grams (g) and kilograms (kg); calculate and solve problems involving mass; convert between g and kg (limited to whole numbers and common fractions).
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 4 mass worksheets: reading scales, grams and kilograms, converting, comparing masses and problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Change to the same unit before comparing.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • We measure mass in grams (g) and kilograms (kg). 1 000 g = 1 kg.
  • Light things like a slice of bread are measured in grams; heavy things like a bag of mealie meal in kilograms.
  • Read a scale carefully: find what each small mark stands for.
  • Before you compare, change both masses to the same unit.

Examples

Example

2 kg 350 g

2 kg = 2 000 g

2 000 + 350

Answer: 2 350 g

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Wrong marksCount what each mark is worth.
100 g in a kilogram1 kg = 1 000 g.
Different unitsChange to the same unit first.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 4 say about mass?
faq.a: Estimate, measure, record, compare and order the mass of objects using bathroom scales, kitchen scales and balances, in grams and kilograms, and convert between g and kg.

faq.q: How heavy is a 1 litre bottle of water?
Is mass the same as weight?
faq.a: In everyday language we say weight, but in maths we measure mass.

faq.q: What scale is used for people?

items.q: How many grams are in half a kilogram?
items.e: 1 kg = 1 000 g. Half of 1 000 is 500, so half a kilogram is 500 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a bunch of grapes. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 g ÷ 4 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 200 g: 250 g. So it is 250 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a bag of potatoes. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 g ÷ 4 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 600 g: 650 g. So it is 650 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a tub of yoghurt. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 g ÷ 4 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 800 g: 850 g. So it is 850 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a block of cheese. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 g. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 g ÷ 5 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 250 g: 300 g, 350 g. So it is 350 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a bag of rice. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 g. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 g ÷ 5 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 500 g: 550 g, 600 g. So it is 600 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a bag of oranges. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 g. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 g ÷ 5 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 750 g: 800 g, 850 g, 900 g. So it is 900 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a pineapple. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 g. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 500 g ÷ 5 = 100 g. Count the spaces after 1 000 g: 1 100 g, 1 200 g, 1 300 g. So it is 1 300 g.

items.q: The needle is halfway between two marks. What is the mass of the bag of flour?
items.e: Each mark is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 g. The needle is halfway between 400 g and 500 g. Halfway between them is 450 g.

items.q: The scales show the mass of a bag of potting mix. What is the mass?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 4 spaces, so each mark is 1 000 ÷ 4 = 250 g. The needle is 3 marks past 2 kg: 3 × 250 = 750 g. So it is 2 kg 750 g.

items.q: The scales show the mass of a watermelon. What is the mass?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 2 spaces, so each mark is 1 000 ÷ 2 = 500 g. The needle is 1 mark past 3 kg: 1 × 500 = 500 g. So it is 3 kg 500 g.
Each kilogram is split into 10 spaces, so each mark is 1 000 ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 8 marks past 1 kg: 8 × 100 = 800 g. So it is 1 kg 800 g.

items.q: The scales show the mass of a bag of dog food. What is the mass?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 4 spaces, so each mark is 1 000 ÷ 4 = 250 g. The needle is 1 mark past 4 kg: 1 × 250 = 250 g. So it is 4 kg 250 g.
Each kilogram is split into 10 spaces, so each mark is 1 000 ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 6 marks past 2 kg: 6 × 100 = 600 g. So it is 2 kg 600 g.

items.q: Pieter stands on the bathroom scales. What is his mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 5 kg. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 5 kg ÷ 5 = 1 kg. Count the spaces after 30 kg: 31 kg, 32 kg, 33 kg. So it is 33 kg.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a block of cheese. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 g. The needle is 1 mark past 200: 200 + 100 = 300 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bunch of bananas. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 g. The needle is 1 mark past 600: 600 + 100 = 700 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of apples. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 g. The needle is 1 mark past 800: 800 + 100 = 900 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a tub of yoghurt. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 g. The needle is 1 mark past 400: 400 + 100 = 500 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a loaf of bread. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 g. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 g. The needle is 3 marks past 500: 500 + 300 = 800 g.
1 000 g = 1 kg. How many groups of 1 000 are in 7 000? 7 000 ÷ 1 000 = 7, so it is 7 kg.
1 000 g = 1 kg. How many groups of 1 000 are in 3 000? 3 000 ÷ 1 000 = 3, so it is 3 kg.

items.q: Look at the pan balance. Which object is lighter?
items.e: The pan with the jar of jam is lower, so the jar is heavier and the beach ball is lighter. The beach ball is big, but it is full of air.

items.q: Which is heavier: 1 kg or 900 g?
items.e: Change to the same unit: 1 kg = 1 000 g. 1 000 g is more than 900 g, so 1 kg is heavier. A bigger number is not always more.

items.q: Which is heavier: 3 kg or 2 500 g?
items.e: 3 kg = 3 000 g. 3 000 g is more than 2 500 g, so 3 kg is heavier.

items.q: Look at the pan balance. Which object is heavier?
items.e: The pan with the brick is lower, so the brick is heavier. The pillow is bigger, but a bigger object is not always heavier.

items.q: 5 kg = ☐ g
2 kg = ☐ g
Which fact about mass is true?
items.e: Kilo means 1 000. One kilogram is 1 000 grams.

items.q: Half of a kilogram is how many grams?
items.e: 1 kg = 1 000 g. Half of 1 000 is 500, so half a kilogram is 500 g. (50 g would be half of 100 g.)

items.q: 10 kg = ☐ g
2 kg 400 g = ☐ g
3 kg 50 g = ☐ g
items.e: 3 kg = 3 000 g. Add the 50 g: 3 000 + 50 = 3 050 g. Writing 3 500 g would add 500 g, not 50 g.
1,5 kg is 1 kg and half a kilogram (5 tenths). 1 000 g + 500 g = 1 500 g.

items.q: 15 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 15 of 1 000 g = 1 000 ÷ 5 = 200 g.

items.q: How many kilograms are in 9 000 g?

items.e: 1 000 g = 1 kg, with 310 g left: 1 kg 310 g.

items.q: Convert 5 kg 626 g to g.

items.e: 6 000 g = 6 kg, with 360 g left: 6 kg 360 g.

items.q: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
items.e: Kilo means 1 000, so 1 kg = 1 000 g.

items.q: About what is the mass of a bag of sugar?
items.e: A bag of sugar is about 1 kilogram (1 000 g). 1 g is about the mass of a paper clip.

items.q: Convert. 5 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1 000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so you need more grams: multiply. 5 × 1 000 = 5 000, so 5 kg = 5 000 g.

items.q: Convert. 3 000 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1 000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so you need fewer kilograms: divide. 3 000 ÷ 1 000 = 3, so 3 000 g = 3 kg.

items.q: Convert. 2 kg 300 g = ☐ g
Convert. 2 kg 30 g = ☐ g
items.e: 2 kg = 2 000 g. Add the 30 g: 2 000 + 30 = 2 030 g. Writing 230 g forgets that 2 kg is 2 000 g.

items.q: Which is the same as 3 450 g?
items.e: 1 000 g = 1 kg, so 3 000 g = 3 kg. 3 450 g = 3 kg and 450 g left over.
The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 4 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 200 ÷ 4 = 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 600 g: 600 + 50 = 650 g.

items.q: Convert 4 kg 584 g to g.
How many kilograms are in 6 000 g?
14 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 14 of 1 000 g = 1 000 ÷ 4 = 250 g.

items.q: Convert 9 kg to g.
12 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 12 of 1 000 g = 1 000 ÷ 2 = 500 g.

items.q: Convert 4 kg 375 g to g.

items.e: 8 000 g = 8 kg, with 10 g left: 8 kg 10 g.

items.q: Convert 2 kg to g.
How many kilograms are in 8 000 g?

items.e: 2 000 g = 2 kg, with 125 g left: 2 kg 125 g.
9 000 g = 9 kg, with 765 g left: 9 kg 765 g.
9 000 g = 9 kg, with 80 g left: 9 kg 80 g.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of a bag of sugar?
items.e: A bag of sugar is about 1 kilogram. 1 g is about the mass of a paper clip.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of an apple?
items.e: An apple is light, about 100 grams. 100 kg is heavier than a grown-up.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of a Grade 3 child?
items.e: A Grade 3 child is about 25 kilograms. 25 g is lighter than a bar of chocolate.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of carrots. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 300: 300 + 50 = 350 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of an apple. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 100: 100 + 50 = 150 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a jar of honey. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 400: 400 + 50 = 450 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a box of cereal. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 g. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 g. The needle is 4 marks past 0: 400 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of potatoes. What is the mass?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 2 equal spaces. 1 kg = 1 000 g, so each mark is 1 000 ÷ 2 = 500 g. The needle is 1 mark past 2 kg: 2 kg + 500 g = 2 kg 500 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a pumpkin. What is the mass?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 2 equal spaces. 1 kg = 1 000 g, so each mark is 1 000 ÷ 2 = 500 g. The needle is 1 mark past 1 kg: 1 kg + 500 g = 1 kg 500 g.
Each kilogram is split into 10 equal spaces. 1 kg = 1 000 g, so each mark is 1 000 ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 3 marks past 1 kg: 1 kg + 300 g = 1 kg 300 g.
Each kilogram is split into 10 equal spaces. 1 kg = 1 000 g, so each mark is 1 000 ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 7 marks past 2 kg: 2 kg + 700 g = 2 kg 700 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of dog food. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 2 kg. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. The needle is 1 mark past 6 kg: 6 kg + 1 kg = 7 kg.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a pile of books. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 2 kg. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. The needle is 1 mark past 2 kg: 2 kg + 1 kg = 3 kg.

items.q: The scale shows a bag of flour. How much more flour is needed to make 1 kg?
items.e: The needle is at 600 g. 1 kg = 1 000 g. 1 000 − 600 = 400 g more.

items.q: The scale shows a bowl of cherries. The empty bowl weighs 100 g. What is the mass of the cherries?
items.e: Each mark is 50 g, so the needle is at 250 g. Take away the bowl: 250 − 100 = 150 g.

items.q: Dumisani buys 3 kg of potatoes and 600 g of onions. What is the total mass in grams?
Ravi buys 3 kg of potatoes and 500 g of onions. What is the total mass in grams?
A bag of mealie meal has a mass of 8 kg. Megan uses 500 g for supper. How much is left?
A bag of mealie meal has a mass of 2 kg. Naledi uses 500 g for supper. How much is left?
Tebogo buys 9 kg of potatoes and 450 g of onions. What is the total mass in grams?
Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 1 kg 500 g = 1 500 g and 1 kg 50 g = 1 050 g. 1 500 g is the most. Do not compare only the numbers 1 and 1 450.
Each mark is 1 000 ÷ 4 = 250 g. A shows 2 kg 750 g and B shows 3 kg 250 g. B is heavier. From 2 kg 750 g to 3 kg is 250 g, and to 3 kg 250 g is 250 g more: 500 g.

items.q: Which list goes from the coldest to the warmest?
items.e: Below zero is colder than 0 °C. −2 °C is the coldest, then 0 °C, then 3 °C.

items.q: Mum stands on the bathroom scales: 62 kg. Then she picks up the dog and the scales show 71 kg. What is the mass of the dog?
items.e: The dog’s mass is the difference: 71 − 62 = 9 kg.

items.q: The school tuck shop buys 2 kg 500 g of onions for the fundraiser. They use 1 kg 750 g. How much is left?
items.e: Change to grams: 2 500 − 1 750 = 750 g. Do not take 500 from 750: the grams part needs regrouping.

items.q: A sunflower in the school garden is measured with a tape measure. How much more must it grow to be 2 m tall?
items.e: Each mark is 10 ÷ 5 = 2 cm. The pointer is 3 marks past 170: 176 cm. 2 m = 200 cm. 200 − 176 = 24 cm.
